core_obligations: Derive from the characterisation lemmas and the definitions that the space is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 4026-4029).
Apply the structure theorem to write the space as a filtered colimit of thickenings of algebraic spaces (proof lines 4029-4032).

Note that every member of that presentation has the same reduction as the space and hence is affine, and conclude that the space is an affine formal algebraic space by definition (proof lines 4032-4037).
proof_roadmap: Affineness of the members and the conclusion (proof lines 4032-4037).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a formal algebraic space over a scheme is an affine formal algebraic space if and only if its reduction is an affine scheme (statement lines 4017-4024). The proof establishes the two structural properties of the space that the criterion requires: by the two characterisation lemmas for the separated and quasi-compact types and the corresponding definitions, the space is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 4026-4029), and hence admits a presentation as a filtered colimit of thickenings of algebraic spaces by the structure theorem for such spaces (proof lines 4029-4032). Each member of that presentation has the same reduction as the space, so each is affine because a thickening of an affine algebraic space is affine; the presentation therefore exhibits the space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes with thickenings as transition maps, which is precisely the definition of an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 4032-4037). The claim is H2: the argument identifies the two hypotheses of the structure theorem, applies it, and then transfers affineness along the presentation, each step with its reason.
